scope: Validated fresh-produce profiles plus source-backed storage-stability profiles for common Indonesian dry agricultural commodities.
important_note: Reference values are operational storage references, not universal guarantees or spoilage probabilities. Dry commodities use moisture/RH storage-stability thresholds and do not receive fabricated fresh-produce Quality-at-Arrival curves.

profiles.name: Green Coffee
profiles.profile_context: Dried green coffee bean storage and transport profile; not roasted coffee or fresh coffee cherry.

source_references.name: FAO — Coffee quality and storage guidance
source_references.supports: FAO states green coffee moisture for satisfactory storage should not be over 11%; this is used as the conservative AgriFlow storage limit.

source_references.name: FAO — Arabica coffee manual
source_references.supports: Green coffee storage guidance recommends a well-ventilated area below 65% RH and advises against storage longer than 12 months.

source_references.name: International Coffee Organization — Resolution 420
source_references.supports: ICO export quality standard specifies 8–12.5% moisture for Arabica and Robusta. AgriFlow does not treat this wider export-quality band as a universal safe-storage guarantee.

profiles.storage_science_note: AgriFlow uses the stricter FAO 11% storage moisture guidance for the operational storage threshold, while exposing the ICO 8–12.5% export-quality standard as supporting context. RH below 65% and a 12-month maximum reference come from the FAO Arabica manual.
profiles.notes: The alias 'kopi' resolves specifically to dried green coffee bean in this MVP. Roasted coffee and fresh coffee cherry require separate profiles. 'Low' perishability is retained only for legacy compatibility and is not used as a biological spoilage claim.
profiles.source_name: FAO — Green coffee storage guidance

profiles.name: Milled Rice
profiles.profile_context: Milled rice / beras storage profile; paddy or rough rice is intentionally not mapped to this profile.

source_references.name: FAO — Quality assurance of selected commodities
source_references.supports: FAO gives 13% maximum moisture for one year of milled-rice storage at 27°C and 70% RH.

source_references.name: FAO — Rice in human nutrition
source_references.supports: FAO notes 14% as a generally accepted safe-storage moisture level in the tropics and says milled rice may need redrying to 14%.

profiles.storage_science_note: AgriFlow distinguishes a general short-term/tropical 14% storage reference from the stricter 13% one-year FAO guideline at 27°C and 70% RH.
profiles.notes: The aliases 'rice' and 'beras' resolve to milled rice. 'Padi', 'paddy', and 'rough rice' are deliberately excluded because their safe-storage characteristics differ.
profiles.source_name: FAO — Milled rice safe-storage guidance

profiles.name: Paddy Rice
profiles.profile_context: Dried paddy/rough rice storage profile; not milled rice.

source_references.name: FAO — Quality assurance of selected commodities
source_references.supports: FAO guideline table gives 15% maximum moisture for one year of paddy storage at 27°C and 70% RH.

source_references.name: FAO — Prevention of post-harvest food losses
source_references.supports: FAO equilibrium table lists paddy at 14% moisture at 70% RH and 27°C.

profiles.storage_science_note: The dataset stores 15% as the short/reference ceiling from the one-year grain table and 14% as the more conservative long-term/equilibrium reference.
profiles.notes: This profile represents the named dried/storage form only. Fresh, wet, processed, roasted, or otherwise different forms require separate profiles.
profiles.source_name: FAO — Paddy storage moisture guidance

profiles.name: Dried Maize Kernels
profiles.profile_context: Shelled, dried maize grain storage profile; not fresh sweet corn.

source_references.name: FAO — Quality assurance of selected commodities
source_references.supports: FAO gives 13.5% maximum moisture for one year of maize storage at 27°C and 70% RH.

source_references.name: FAO — Maize marketing guide
source_references.supports: FAO states ideal moisture for storing maize is below 13% and highlights faster deterioration as moisture rises.

profiles.storage_science_note: AgriFlow uses 13.5% as the cited one-year guideline and 13% as the more conservative long-term operational threshold.
profiles.notes: This profile represents the named dried/storage form only. Fresh, wet, processed, roasted, or otherwise different forms require separate profiles.
profiles.source_name: FAO — Maize safe-storage guidance

profiles.name: Soybeans

source_references.name: FAO — Technology of production of edible flours and protein products from soybeans
source_references.supports: FAO says soybeans should be about 12–13% moisture for good storage stability and viability; above this mould risk becomes serious, especially in hot weather.

source_references.name: FAO — Soybean Post-Harvest Compendium
source_references.supports: FAO table reports soybean equilibrium moisture around 11–12% at 65–70% RH and 25°C.

profiles.storage_science_note: The short-term ceiling is 13%; the long-term conservative reference is 12%. RH 70% is treated as an upper reference boundary, not a universal guarantee.
profiles.notes: This profile represents the named dried/storage form only. Fresh, wet, processed, roasted, or otherwise different forms require separate profiles.
profiles.source_name: FAO — Soybean storage stability guidance

profiles.name: Cocoa Beans

source_references.name: FAO/Codex — Cocoa storage provisions
source_references.supports: Codex/FAO text states cocoa storage should keep bean moisture as low as possible and in any case not above 8.0%.

source_references.name: FAO — Prevention of post-harvest food losses
source_references.supports: FAO equilibrium table lists cocoa beans at 7% moisture at 70% RH and 27°C.

profiles.storage_science_note: AgriFlow uses 8% as the upper short-term/storage provision and 7% as the more conservative equilibrium/long-term reference.
profiles.notes: This profile represents the named dried/storage form only. Fresh, wet, processed, roasted, or otherwise different forms require separate profiles.
profiles.source_name: FAO/Codex — Cocoa storage guidance

source_references.supports: FAO table lists millet at 16% equilibrium moisture content at 27°C and 70% RH.

profiles.storage_science_note: The 16% value is retained only as the cited FAO storage reference and not as a universal spoilage threshold.
profiles.notes: This profile represents the named dried/storage form only. Fresh, wet, processed, roasted, or otherwise different forms require separate profiles.
profiles.source_name: FAO — Millet storage guidance
